milestones.title: M6 Tool library
milestones.description: Tool library after 1.0: E11 to E19, SDS 19

epics.title: Foundation for the tool library
epics.description: The generic machinery that the tools of E13 to E19 need so that each tool is a registry entry plus its geometry and not a new state machine: anchor rules and a kind registry, pane-anchored drawings, placement and editing for many anchors and freehand points, new shape types with hit-testing, host capabilities and series access, a registry-driven catalog with grouped toolbars. It builds on the host contract v3 of E11-F04-S01; record every change in the SDS first (§19).

features.title: Anchor model for the tool library
features.description: Anchor rules and a kind registry, pane-anchored drawings, and the placement and editing of drawings with three or more anchors, a variable number of anchors or freehand points.
features.why: every later tool is built on one generic machine instead of its own state machine

stories.title: Anchor rules and kind registry
stories.userStory: As a maintainer, I want one registry of drawing kinds with anchor rules so that adding a tool is one entry and not a change in six files.
acceptance: `ANCHOR_RULES[kind] = { min, max }` is exported from core; fixed kinds have `min = max`, and `ANCHOR_COUNT` stays, derived from the rules for fixed kinds.
`KFT-E-ANCHORS` names the allowed range in its message.

A registry entry holds the kind, its anchor rule, its option schema and defaults, its geometry function, its hit parts and its catalog group; adding a kind needs no change outside the registry and the geometry module of the kind (a test registers a fake kind to prove it).
The eight kinds of 1.0 are registered through the registry and every existing test passes unchanged; documents of 1.0 load unchanged.
Importing a document with an unknown kind fails with `KFT-E-KIND` for that drawing; `merge` skips and reports it (D-15).
tasks: Define the registry type and `ANCHOR_RULES`.
Move the eight kinds into the registry.
Make `validateDrawing`, the options validation and `geometryOf` read the registry.
Add the fake-kind test and the unknown-kind import tests.

stories.title: Pane-anchored drawings
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want some annotations to stay at a fixed spot of the pane so that a legend or a table does not move when I zoom or scroll.
acceptance: A kind can declare `space: pane`; it stores one anchor that only names the pane (time and price are ignored for the geometry, like D-5) and `options.position = { x, y }` as fractions 0..1 of the pane; a position outside 0..1 fails with `KFT-E-OPTIONS`.
The geometry is placed from `paneRect`, so zoom, scroll and resize keep the position relative to the pane.
Dragging changes the position; the drawing stays at least partly inside the pane (clamped); undo, redo, export and import keep the position.
A pane-anchored drawing of a pane that disappears has no scene item and is kept in the store, like any drawing without a pane.
tasks: Add the `space` flag and the position option to the registry.
Geometry from the pane fractions.
Move and clamp in the interaction engine.
Tests: zoom, scroll, resize, pane removal, round trip.

stories.title: Placement of tools with three or more anchors
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to place channels, pitchforks and patterns with one click per point so that I can draw them as quickly as a trend line.
acceptance: One click per anchor (a tap on touch); the first two anchors also work by drag; the last anchor completes the drawing in one history entry.
The preview shows the anchors placed so far with the pointer as the next anchor; Escape and the right button cancel without a store change.
A point closer than `ZERO_LENGTH_PX` to the previous anchor is ignored and waits for another.
The keyboard cursor places each anchor with Enter (FR-INT-035) and `stayInTool` repeats the tool.
Each step is announced ("Place anchor 3 of 5") through the message table.
tasks: Generalize `PlacementProgress` from two anchors to a list.
Extend `reducePlacement` and the preview for partial anchors.
Add the announcement keys.
Table tests for 3, 4 and 7 anchors; scenario tests for mouse, touch and keyboard.

stories.title: Placement of variable-anchor tools
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to place a polyline point by point and finish it when I decide so that I can trace a formation of any length.
acceptance: A kind with `min < max` anchors takes one click per anchor; Enter or a double click completes it when it has at least `min` anchors.
Backspace removes the last placed anchor; reaching `max` completes the drawing; Escape cancels the whole drawing.
The completed drawing is one history entry and one `created` event; fewer than `min` anchors never creates a drawing.
Touch works: a tap places a point and a double tap or the Enter key of an attached keyboard completes.
tasks: Add the finish rules to the placement reducer.
Add Backspace handling while placing.
Tests for min, max, finish, undo of a point and cancel.

stories.title: Freehand placement
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to draw freely with the pointer or a pen so that I can sketch on the chart.
acceptance: Pointer down starts a stroke; moves add a point at least 3 px from the last; pointer up completes it (touch and pen too); Escape cancels.
On completion the points are simplified (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker, 1 px) and limited to 512 anchors; a stroke of fewer than 2 points creates nothing.
The stroke is one history entry; all points are in data space and keep their `yAxisId` of the first point.
A stroke that leaves the pane is clipped at the pane edge; the points inside are kept.
tasks: Add a freehand placement mode to the interaction engine.
Implement the simplification as a pure function.
Tests for sampling, simplification, cap, cancel and clipping.

stories.title: Handles, move and edit for drawings with many anchors
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to adjust any point of a many-point drawing so that I can correct a pattern without drawing it again.
acceptance: Every anchor has a handle (`handle:<n>`); a kind can add its own handles through the registry.
Dragging a handle moves one anchor; dragging the body moves all anchors; arrow keys nudge as for the existing kinds (FR-INT-034).
Freehand drawings have four bounding-box handles that scale the points about the opposite corner.
A locked drawing refuses every change; a continuous drag is one history entry (FR-HI-003).
tasks: Generalize the handle model in geometry and hit-testing.
Generalize the move and resize reducer.
Add the scale handles for freehand drawings.
Scenario tests for 3, 5 and 64 anchors.

features.title: Shapes, hit-testing and Fibonacci items
features.description: New shape types in geometry and scene, hit-testing for them, and the extension of the Fibonacci scene item and parity fixture for the new Fibonacci kinds.
features.why: the hosts draw only what the scene says, so every new look needs a defined, tested primitive

stories.title: New shape types in geometry and scene
stories.userStory: As a chart developer, I want a small set of new scene shapes so that I can draw every new tool with primitives I already know how to render.
acceptance: `polyline`, `polygon` (closed, fillable), `ellipse`, `curve` (quadratic or cubic Bezier), `arrowhead` and `glyph` (text, emoji or built-in icon) are added to the `Shape` union and documented in SDS §8.3.
Every shape takes stroke, dash, fill and opacity from the resolved style; `buildScene` and `SceneCache` handle them and keep the same-array guarantee of FR-SC-001.
The mock host and the playground host draw the new shapes on canvas; the host guide lists how to render each.
Golden scene tests cover every shape with fill, dash, locked, selected and hover states.
tasks: Extend the `Shape` types and `buildScene`.
Add canvas drawing to the mock and playground hosts.
Update SDS §8.3 and the host guide.
Golden scene tests.

stories.title: Hit-testing for the new shapes
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to select a curve, polygon or ellipse by clicking on it so that the new tools are as easy to pick as the old ones.
acceptance: A polyline is hit by its distance to the segments; a polygon and an ellipse by their outline and, when filled, by their inside; a curve by its flattened path within 0.25 px; a glyph by its box.
The tolerance, the part names (`body`, `handle:<n>`, `level:<ratio>`, `label`) and the tie-breaking of FR-HIT-004 are unchanged.
Property tests show that hit-testing agrees with the geometry for random shapes, and a benchmark with 500 mixed drawings stays within the budget of NFR-PERF-002.
tasks: Distance functions for the new shapes.
Part naming for cells, levels and labels.
Property tests and a benchmark.

stories.title: Fibonacci scene item for the new Fibonacci kinds
stories.userStory: As a chart developer, I want the new Fibonacci kinds in the same scene item as the old ones so that my Fibonacci renderer draws them identically to the programmatic ones.
acceptance: `FibonacciKind` includes the trend-based extension of E11 and the channel, time extension, circles, spiral and wedge of E15; each has fully resolved options in the `fibonacci` item.
`FIBONACCI_PARITY` has cases for every new kind (tolerance 1e-9, labels not part of it) and `FIBONACCI_PARITY_VERSION` is increased once for the set.
The host guide and the chart handoff issue describe the new kinds; a host that does not render a Fibonacci kind reports it in `capabilities` (E12-F03-S01).
tasks: Extend the kind union and the resolved options.
Extend the parity fixture and bump the version.
Update the host guide.

features.title: Host capabilities and series data
features.description: Optional host capabilities so a host can say which shapes it renders and whether it has series data, the series access for the data tools, the pure helpers that compute from it, and the conformance kit and chart handoff for all of it. Builds on the host contract v3 of E11-F04-S01.
features.why: tools that a host cannot draw or feed must be disabled with a clear reason instead of breaking the chart

stories.title: Host capabilities
stories.userStory: As a chart developer, I want to declare what my host can render so that tools I cannot draw yet are disabled and not broken.
acceptance: `DrawingHost` v3 has an optional `capabilities: { shapes?: ShapeType[]; series?: boolean; fibonacci?: FibonacciKind[] }`.
A v3 host without `shapes` is taken to render the shapes of SDS §8.3 as of 1.0 only; a v2 host keeps the eight tools of 1.0.
A tool whose shapes, Fibonacci kind or series the host lacks is disabled in the toolbar; activating it emits `blocked` with `KFT-E-CAPABILITY` listing what is missing.
Drawings of such a tool are kept in the store and the document but have no scene item (FR-TOOL-040).
tasks: Add `capabilities` to the contract and the host check.
Compute the allowed tools from the capabilities.
Add `KFT-E-CAPABILITY` to the diagnostics.
Tests with hosts of version 2 and 3.

stories.title: Series access
stories.userStory: As a chart developer, I want to hand the tools the bars of the visible range so that tools that depend on data can compute without reading chart internals.
acceptance: The optional `seriesBetween(from, to)` returns `readonly Bar[]` with `Bar = { time, open, high, low, close, volume? }`, ascending by time, at most 10 000 bars.
A host that returns more bars, unsorted bars or non-finite values fails the conformance kit with the offending index.
The controller calls it only while a data tool is placing, moving or rendering, and caches the result until the viewport or the data change.
tasks: Define the types and the contract text.
Add the cache with invalidation.
Update the mock host with a configurable series.
Unit tests for limits, ordering and invalidation.

stories.title: Tools that the host cannot serve
stories.userStory: As an application developer, I want a clear behaviour when a stored drawing needs a capability that the host lacks so that no drawing is lost.
acceptance: Stored drawings of a tool whose capability is missing stay in the store, are exported and imported unchanged, and are listed in the diagnostics.
They have no scene item, are not hit-tested and cannot be selected by click; select all does not select them.
When the capability appears (a host is replaced), the drawings render without a reload.
tasks: Filter the scene and hit-test by capability.
Report them in the diagnostics.
Tests for host replacement.

stories.title: Pure helpers for data tools
stories.userStory: As a maintainer, I want the calculations of the data tools as pure, tested functions so that the tools do not depend on the indicators repository and stay exact.
acceptance: Core exports pure helpers: linear regression with standard deviation, volume-weighted average price with optional bands, the volume profile with point of control and value area, and the bar copy for the bars pattern.
Each helper has golden numbers from an independent calculation (1e-9) and property tests for empty, single-bar and flat inputs.
No import from keystone-financial-indicators exists (dependency rule of §4.2 is checked).
tasks: Implement the four helpers.
Golden fixtures and property tests.
Dependency check in the architecture test.

stories.title: Conformance kit and chart handoff for the new contract parts
stories.userStory: As a chart developer, I want the conformance kit to check capabilities, new shapes and series so that I can prove my host is correct.
acceptance: `runHostConformance` checks `capabilities`, the rendering of every declared shape through a golden scene, and `seriesBetween` when declared.
A failing check names the contract member that differs.
The host guide is updated and a new issue in gwinnem/keystone-charts-financial links this epic and lists the shapes, the series and the Fibonacci kinds that the chart should implement.
tasks: Extend the kit and the golden scenes.
Update the host guide.
Open and link the chart issue.

features.title: Catalog, options and toolbar groups
features.description: A catalog driven by the registry with more groups, a `tools` option with a safe default, messages and announcements for every new tool, a headless grouped toolbar model, and the adapters, docs and playground for it.
features.why: a toolbar with about 90 tools must be grouped, translatable and opt-in

stories.title: Catalog groups from the registry
stories.userStory: As an application developer, I want the catalog to list every registered tool in groups so that I can build a grouped toolbar.
acceptance: `ToolGroup` gains `channels`, `pitchforks`, `gann`, `measure` and `patterns` next to `lines`, `shapes`, `fibonacci` and `annotations`; the order of the catalog is the order of the groups.
`ToolCatalogEntry` gains `requires` (`series`, shapes, Fibonacci kinds) from the registry; `tier` stays information only (D-14).
The catalog of the eight tools of 1.0 is unchanged in content and order.
tasks: Derive the catalog from the registry.
Add the groups and `requires`.
Catalog tests including the unchanged first eight.

stories.title: The `tools` option and its default
stories.userStory: As an application developer, I want to choose which tools my users get so that adding tools to the package never changes my toolbar by surprise.
acceptance: The default of the `tools` option stays the eight tools of 1.0; a list of ids or the value `all` enables others.
An unknown id is ignored and reported in the diagnostics; a tool is `enabled` only when it is in the option and the host has its capabilities.
The option is reactive in the adapters like today.
tasks: Extend the option parsing and resolution.
Wire the capability check into `enabled`.
Tests for default, list, `all`, unknown ids and capabilities.

stories.title: Messages and announcements for the new tools
stories.userStory: As a screen reader user and as a translator, I want every new tool to have a label and announcements in the message table so that nothing is hard coded.
acceptance: The message table has a `tool.<kind>` key for every registered kind, a `group.<name>` key for every group and keys for the step announcements and `KFT-E-CAPABILITY`.
Announcements use the placeholders already supported; the placeholder lists of the existing tests are updated.
A test fails when a registered kind has no label or when a message key is unused.
tasks: Add the keys and defaults.
Add the completeness test.
Update the docs table of messages.

stories.title: Headless grouped toolbar model
stories.userStory: As an application developer, I want the toolbar as groups with a remembered tool per group so that I can build a flyout toolbar without writing the logic.
acceptance: The state has `toolbarGroups`: for each group its entries, the entry shown on the group button (the last used, else the first enabled) and whether the group has an active tool.
Activating a tool updates the remembered tool of its group; the memory is per controller and is reset by `dispose`.
The flat `toolbar` array of 1.0 is unchanged.
tasks: Define the group state and the reducer.
Expose it in the controller state.
Tests for remembering, disabled groups and reset.

stories.title: Adapters, docs and playground for the grouped toolbar
stories.userStory: As a Vue, React or Angular developer, I want the grouped toolbar in my framework so that I can offer the whole library with a flyout toolbar.
acceptance: The Vue and React composables and the Angular service expose `toolbarGroups` and re-export every new core export; the parity test passes.
The toolbar guide has a grouped toolbar example for each framework and lists every tool with its group, anchors and requirements.
The playground offers a flyout toolbar with a switch for `tools: all`; Playwright covers opening a group, choosing a tool and placing it in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
tasks: Expose the model in the three adapters.
Write the guide.
Build the playground toolbar.
Add the e2e scenarios.

epics.title: Lines and markers
epics.description: The remaining line and marker kinds of the competing products after the vertical line, ray, extended line and arrows of E11: the horizontal ray, the cross line, the measuring lines and the side arrows and flag. All are one- or two-anchor kinds on the generic machine of E12.

features.title: Horizontal ray and cross line
features.description: Two one-anchor line kinds that reuse the price label of the horizontal line.
features.why: support and resistance that start at a bar, and a pair of lines that mark one exact moment and level

stories.title: Horizontal ray
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to draw a horizontal ray that starts at a bar and runs to the right so that I can mark a level that only matters from a given moment.
acceptance: `horizontal-ray` is a drawing kind with 1 anchor in `ANCHOR_RULES` and in `DRAWING_KINDS`; another anchor count fails with `KFT-E-ANCHORS`, and a document with the kind round-trips through export and import.

Geometry: a horizontal segment at the anchor price from the anchor time to the right edge of the pane, with the price label of the horizontal line (FR-SC-001). The geometry is pure and deterministic and has golden tests, including reversed anchors, anchors outside the pane and a drawing of zero size.
The kind has no kind options of its own (`options` on it fail with `KFT-E-OPTIONS`); style values resolve from the theme at scene time (FR-DM-011).
Hit-testing: the line, its price label (`label`) and the handle at the anchor; a hidden drawing is not hit.
Placement is one click or tap (FR-INT-010); Escape cancels, `stayInTool` repeats the tool and the finished drawing is one history entry.
Move, resize through the handles, nudge, duplicate, lock, hide, z-order, delete and undo/redo work as for the existing tools, and a locked drawing refuses them.
Scene: one `shape` item with the line and the price label text

Catalog: an entry in the group `lines` with the label key `tool.horizontal-ray`, an icon name and no default shortcut; the tier is information only (D-14); the message table, the announcements and the three adapters expose it and the parity test passes.
Documentation and tests: the toolbar guide and the docs entry describe the tool, the playground can place it, and one e2e test places it, moves it, undoes the move and deletes it.
tasks: Add `horizontal-ray` to the registry: kind, anchor rule, kind options and validation.
Geometry, handles and hit parts in core, and the scene output.
Placement, move and resize through the generic machine of E12 (no tool-specific state machine).
Catalog entry, message keys, announcements and adapter exports.
Unit tests (golden geometry, hit-testing, placement, move, validation), e2e scenario, docs entry, playground button and CHANGELOG.

features.title: Measuring lines
features.description: The info line and the trend angle: a segment with the numbers a trader reads from it.
features.why: a trend line that tells the move, the percent and the angle without a second tool

stories.title: Info line
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to draw a line that shows its price change, percent, bars and angle so that I read the size of a move while I draw it.
acceptance: `info-line` is a drawing kind with 2 anchors in `ANCHOR_RULES` and in `DRAWING_KINDS`; another anchor count fails with `KFT-E-ANCHORS`, and a document with the kind round-trips through export and import.

Geometry: a segment from anchor 1 to anchor 2 with an info box near anchor 2 showing the price change, the percent change, the number of bars (time span divided by `barInterval`) and the angle in degrees. The geometry is pure and deterministic and has golden tests, including reversed anchors, anchors outside the pane and a drawing of zero size.

Options: `showPrice`, `showPercent`, `showBars`, `showAngle` (booleans, default true). Invalid values, and these options on another kind, fail with `KFT-E-OPTIONS`; unset style values resolve from the theme at scene time (FR-DM-011).
Hit-testing: the segment, the info box (`label`) and one handle per anchor; a hidden drawing is not hit.
Placement follows FR-INT-010..014: click-click or drag, the preview follows the pointer, Escape or the right button cancels without a store change, and the finished drawing is one history entry.
Move, resize through the handles, nudge, duplicate, lock, hide, z-order, delete and undo/redo work as for the existing tools, and a locked drawing refuses them.
Scene: shape items for the segment and the box, with the text measured by `measureText` when the host gives one
The angle is measured in pixel space, like the Fibonacci arcs (FR-GEO-005), so it changes with the zoom aspect; the docs say so.

Catalog: an entry in the group `lines` with the label key `tool.info-line`, an icon name and no default shortcut; the tier is information only (D-14); the message table, the announcements and the three adapters expose it and the parity test passes.
Documentation and tests: the toolbar guide and the docs entry describe the tool, the playground can place it, and one e2e test places it, moves it, undoes the move and deletes it.

stories.title: Flag mark
stories.userStory: As a trader, I want to plant a flag on a bar with an optional caption so that I can mark key events on the chart.
